title: English Practice Exam 2024
description: English Practice Exam 2024 - 100 multiple choice questions. Ethiopian national exam preparation material.

questions.questionText: The laboratory lights are on, and the technician's car is outside. She _____ be inside.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion, so must expresses strong present deduction.

questions.questionText: Nobody has seen Daniel today, but his phone is connected to the office Wi-Fi. He _____ be working there.
questions.explanation: The evidence suggests a possibility but does not prove it, so might is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The office is completely locked, and the security guard confirmed that everyone left. They _____ be inside.
questions.explanation: The evidence makes their being inside impossible or extremely unlikely, so can't expresses negative deduction.

questions.questionText: The weather forecast is uncertain, so it _____ rain this afternoon.
questions.explanation: Might expresses an uncertain possibility.

questions.questionText: The examination begins at eight, so the students _____ be in the examination hall by now.
questions.explanation: Should expresses an expected or probable present situation.

questions.questionText: The door is open, but nobody is answering. They _____ be sleeping.
questions.explanation: May expresses a possible explanation for the situation.

questions.questionText: The road is completely flooded. The bridge _____ be safe to cross.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly suggests that the bridge is not safe, so can't expresses negative deduction.

questions.questionText: She has not answered any messages all morning. She _____ be busy.
questions.explanation: The evidence gives a possible explanation, but not a certain conclusion.

questions.questionText: The ground is wet even though nobody watered the garden. It _____ have rained.
questions.explanation: The wet ground is strong evidence that rain occurred, so must have rained expresses past deduction.

questions.questionText: James arrived two hours late. He _____ have missed the earlier bus.
questions.explanation: Missing the earlier bus is one possible explanation, so may have missed is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The lights were switched off when I arrived, but the door was unlocked. The owner _____ have left recently.
questions.explanation: The evidence allows this as a possible past explanation, so might have left works.

questions.questionText: Sara was with me throughout the entire evening. She _____ have committed the crime at 9 p.m.
questions.explanation: Being with the speaker provides strong evidence that the past event was impossible, so couldn't have committed is correct.

questions.questionText: He looks exhausted after working a twelve-hour shift. He _____ be tired.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that he is tired.

questions.questionText: The manager's office is empty, but her computer is still running. She _____ have gone out briefly.
questions.explanation: Going out briefly is a possible explanation, so might have gone is suitable.

questions.questionText: The train has already departed, so the passengers _____ have missed it.
questions.explanation: May have missed expresses a possible past event.

questions.questionText: The entire street is covered in snow. It _____ have snowed heavily during the night.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that heavy snow occurred.

questions.questionText: He is currently in Nairobi, so he _____ be attending the meeting in Addis Ababa at this moment.
questions.explanation: His location provides strong evidence that he cannot be at the meeting.

questions.questionText: The baby is unusually quiet. She _____ be sleeping.
questions.explanation: Sleeping is a possible explanation, so might be sleeping is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The computer is still warm and the document is open. Someone _____ have been using it recently.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly indicates recent use, so must have been using expresses strong deduction.

questions.questionText: The children are not in the classroom, but their bags are on the desks. They _____ be outside.
questions.explanation: Being outside is one possible explanation, so might be outside is correct.

questions.questionText: The package was sent five days ago. It _____ arrive tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Should expresses an expected or probable future result.

questions.questionText: The professor has not arrived yet, but the lecture starts in five minutes. He _____ arrive soon.
questions.explanation: Should expresses expectation or probability.

questions.questionText: The students have been studying since early morning. They _____ be exhausted by now.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that they are exhausted.

questions.questionText: The lights in the house are off, but someone may still be inside. They _____ be asleep.
questions.explanation: Might expresses a tentative possibility.

questions.questionText: There is no sign of John at the station. He _____ have taken a different train.
questions.explanation: Taking a different train is one possible explanation.

questions.questionText: She knew the meeting had been cancelled, so she _____ have gone to the office for it.
questions.explanation: The evidence makes it impossible or extremely unlikely that she went there for the meeting.

questions.questionText: The roads are unusually quiet tonight. There _____ be fewer people travelling because of the storm.
questions.explanation: Fewer travellers is a possible explanation, so might is suitable.

questions.questionText: The electricity has been off for six hours. The refrigerator _____ still be working normally.
questions.explanation: The lack of electricity makes normal operation impossible or extremely unlikely.

questions.questionText: The students have already submitted their papers. They _____ have finished the examination.
questions.explanation: Submission of the papers provides strong evidence that they finished.

questions.questionText: The weather radar shows a large storm approaching. It _____ rain heavily tonight.
questions.explanation: Heavy rain is a possible future situation, so could expresses possibility.

questions.questionText: The museum normally closes at six, so it _____ be open at eight unless there is a special event.
questions.explanation: Under the stated normal circumstances, being open at eight is strongly ruled out.

questions.questionText: I cannot find my keys anywhere. I _____ have left them at the restaurant.
questions.explanation: Leaving them at the restaurant is a possible past explanation.

questions.questionText: Her suitcase is missing from the room. She _____ have taken it with her.
questions.explanation: Taking the suitcase is a possible explanation, so may have taken is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The witness saw the suspect in another city at the exact time of the robbery. He _____ have committed the robbery then.
questions.explanation: The evidence makes the past event impossible or extremely unlikely.

questions.questionText: The children are making no noise, and their bedroom door is closed. They _____ be sleeping.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the deduction that they are sleeping.

questions.questionText: The roads are wet, but the weather report says it has not rained in the area. Someone _____ have washed the roads.
questions.explanation: Washing the roads is a possible explanation, so might have washed is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The office lights are off and the doors are locked. The employees _____ have gone home.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that they went home.

questions.questionText: The manager has not replied to the message. She _____ be in a meeting.
questions.explanation: Being in a meeting is a possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The entire team has disappeared from the building. They _____ be attending the emergency meeting.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports this present deduction.

questions.questionText: The plane left at noon, and the airport records show that she checked in. She _____ have boarded the plane.
questions.explanation: The available evidence strongly supports the conclusion that she boarded.

questions.questionText: Nobody knows where Ahmed is. He _____ have gone to the library.
questions.explanation: Going to the library is one possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The lights in the laboratory are on, but the laboratory is normally closed at night. A researcher _____ be working late.
questions.explanation: Working late is a possible explanation for the lights being on.

questions.questionText: The car is still in the garage, so its owner _____ have driven it to work this morning.
questions.explanation: The car remaining in the garage strongly contradicts the idea that the owner drove it.

questions.questionText: The students look confused because the instructions were unclear. They _____ have misunderstood the question.
questions.explanation: Misunderstanding the question is a possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The package has not arrived after three weeks. It _____ have been lost in the mail.
questions.explanation: Being lost is a possible explanation for the delay.

questions.questionText: The lights are on, the door is open, and music is playing. Someone _____ be inside.
questions.explanation: Several pieces of evidence strongly support the conclusion that someone is inside.

questions.questionText: The security camera shows that the gate was never opened. The suspect _____ have entered through that gate.
questions.explanation: The evidence makes entering through that gate impossible or extremely unlikely.

questions.questionText: The clouds are extremely dark, and a storm warning has been issued. It _____ rain soon.
questions.explanation: Rain is a strong possibility, so could is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The road is blocked by a fallen tree. The bus _____ arrive on time.
questions.explanation: The obstruction makes arriving on time impossible or extremely unlikely.

questions.questionText: The doctor has examined the patient and found a high fever. The patient _____ be suffering from an infection.
questions.explanation: An infection is a possible explanation, so might be is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The student's desk is covered with books and notes. He _____ be preparing for the examination.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the deduction that he is preparing.

questions.questionText: The bus was delayed by an accident. We _____ arrive later than expected.
questions.explanation: Arriving later is a possible consequence of the accident.

questions.questionText: The shop has been closed all day. The owner _____ be away.
questions.explanation: The owner's absence is a possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The report contains several pages of calculations. The researcher _____ have spent many hours preparing it.
questions.explanation: The report provides strong evidence for the deduction that considerable time was spent preparing it.

questions.questionText: The phone has been switched off since yesterday. She _____ be avoiding calls.
questions.explanation: Avoiding calls is one possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The classroom windows are open and the curtains are moving. Someone _____ have opened them.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly suggests that someone opened the windows.

questions.questionText: The road signs indicate that the highway is closed. We _____ use that route tonight.
questions.explanation: The closure strongly indicates that using the route is impossible or not possible under the circumstances.

questions.questionText: The child has been awake since dawn. He _____ be tired now.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that he is tired.

questions.questionText: The meeting ended at four, but Sarah has not returned yet. She _____ have gone somewhere else afterward.
questions.explanation: Going somewhere else is a possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The lights in the stadium are off and the gates are locked. The match _____ be taking place now.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly indicates that the match is not taking place.

questions.questionText: The professor's car is outside his house, but nobody has seen him. He _____ be at home.
questions.explanation: Being at home is possible, but the evidence does not establish it with certainty.

questions.questionText: The student received a very high mark after studying all weekend. She _____ have prepared thoroughly.
questions.explanation: The result and previous information strongly support this past deduction.

questions.questionText: The witness was abroad during the entire month. He _____ have seen the incident in person.
questions.explanation: Being abroad during the entire period makes personally seeing the incident impossible or extremely unlikely.

questions.questionText: The package tracking system says 'out for delivery.' The package _____ arrive today.
questions.explanation: Should expresses an expected or probable result.

questions.questionText: The weather is changing rapidly. The flight _____ be delayed.
questions.explanation: A delay is a possible future event.

questions.questionText: The laboratory was locked from the outside all night. Nobody _____ have entered through the main door.
questions.explanation: The locked door provides strong evidence that entering through it was impossible.

questions.questionText: The children have left their shoes by the swimming pool. They _____ be swimming now.
questions.explanation: The shoes provide strong evidence supporting the deduction that they are swimming.

questions.questionText: The teacher is not in the classroom, and her car is missing. She _____ have gone home.
questions.explanation: Going home is a possible past explanation.

questions.questionText: The workers have been drilling since morning. They _____ be exhausted.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that they are exhausted.

questions.questionText: The computer screen is still active, but the employee is not at the desk. He _____ be taking a break.
questions.explanation: Taking a break is one possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The streets were completely dry at midnight, but they are flooded now. It _____ have rained heavily overnight.
questions.explanation: The change from dry to flooded strongly supports the deduction that heavy rain occurred.

questions.questionText: The suspect was recorded entering the building at 8:00, while the crime occurred at 9:00. He _____ have been inside the building at 9:00.
questions.explanation: The available evidence does not allow the conclusion that he was outside; however, if the context states he left before 9, can't would be needed. Here the sentence does not establish that, so this option is not sufficiently supported.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a strong deduction about the present?
questions.explanation: A modal is followed by the base form, and be is required before an adjective.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a possible past event?
questions.explanation: The correct perfect modal structure is might + have + V3.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a strong deduction about a past event?
options: They must to have gone home.
questions.explanation: Past deduction uses must + have + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a negative deduction about the present?
options: She can't to be at home.
questions.explanation: Can't be is the standard structure for strong negative present deduction.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a possible ongoing action?
questions.explanation: Present continuous possibility uses modal + be + V-ing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a strong deduction about an ongoing past action?
questions.explanation: Past continuous deduction uses must + have been + V-ing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence expresses general possibility rather than a specific uncertain event?
options: She can be at home tonight.
questions.explanation: Can commonly expresses general or theoretical possibility.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best expresses a specific uncertain future possibility?
questions.explanation: May is a standard modal for specific uncertain future possibility.

questions.questionText: Which sentence expresses expectation rather than a very strong deduction?
options: She must be home by now.
She should be home by now.
She can't be home by now.
She couldn't be home by now.
questions.explanation: Should expresses an expected or probable situation and is weaker than must.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly distinguishes deduction from obligation?
options: You must be tired after the journey.
You must to be tired after the journey.
You must being tired after the journey.
You must have to be tired after the journey.
questions.explanation: Must be can express a strong logical deduction based on evidence.

questions.questionText: Which sentence expresses prohibition rather than negative deduction?
questions.explanation: Mustn't expresses prohibition, whereas can't is used for negative deduction.

questions.questionText: Which sentence expresses a possible past explanation?
options: He must have missed the bus.
He might have missed the bus.
He can't have missed the bus.
He should have missed the bus.
questions.explanation: Might have missed expresses uncertainty about what happened.

questions.questionText: Which sentence expresses an unrealized past possibility?
options: He could have won the race, but he fell.
He could be winning the race now.
questions.explanation: The sentence states that winning was possible but did not happen.

questions.questionText: Which sentence most clearly expresses a possible explanation?
options: The lights are off. They could be asleep.
The lights are off. They must be asleep.
The lights are off. They can't be asleep.
The lights are off. They should be asleep.
questions.explanation: Could presents being asleep as one possible explanation.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a negative deduction about a past event?
questions.explanation: Negative past deduction uses can't + have + V3.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses past ongoing possibility?
questions.explanation: Past continuous possibility uses may + have been + V-ing.

questions.questionText: The lights have been on all night, but nobody answers the door. The residents _____ have been sleeping.
questions.explanation: Sleeping is a possible explanation, so might have been sleeping is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The workers' tools are still on the site, and their cars are parked outside. They _____ have left for the day.
questions.explanation: The evidence makes it possible that they have not left, so might not have left is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The alarm is ringing, but nobody is answering the phone. The security guard _____ be investigating it.
questions.explanation: Investigating the alarm is one possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The student submitted an empty answer sheet. He _____ have understood the questions.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly suggests that he did not understand the questions.

questions.questionText: The car's engine is still warm even though the driver is absent. He _____ have driven it recently.
questions.explanation: The warm engine provides strong evidence of recent driving.

questions.questionText: The student is not answering because his phone is switched off. He _____ be studying without interruptions.
questions.explanation: Studying without interruptions is a possible explanation.

questions.questionText: The teacher has already marked all the papers. She _____ have worked for several hours.
questions.explanation: The completed work strongly supports the deduction that she worked for several hours.

questions.questionText: The restaurant is full and people are waiting outside. The food _____ be popular.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that the food is popular.

questions.questionText: The student's computer has crashed, so he _____ have lost some of his work.
questions.explanation: Losing some work is a possible consequence of the crash.

questions.questionText: The road is empty even though it is normally busy at this hour. There _____ be an accident ahead.
questions.explanation: An accident is a possible explanation for the unusual traffic conditions.

questions.questionText: The house has been dark and locked for several days. The owners _____ be away.
questions.explanation: Being away is a possible explanation, but the evidence does not prove it.

questions.questionText: The examination hall is empty and all the answer sheets have been collected. The examination _____ have ended.
questions.explanation: The evidence strongly supports the conclusion that the examination has ended.
